chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said on the occasion of some feast days:
It is truly an 'Eid for him whose fasting Allah accepts and for whose standing (in prayer) He is grateful; and every day in which Allah is not disobeyed is an 'Eid.
ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of Eid in Shia Islam according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) redefines 'Eid from a fixed calendar event to a spiritual state contingent upon the acceptance (Qabul) of fasting and night prayer, a concept central to Shia theological discourse on the efficacy of worship. He further universalizes this joy by declaring any day devoid of sin as an 'Eid, thereby encouraging believers to maintain a continuous state of piety rather than limiting celebration to specific festivals.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 428. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said on the occcasion of an ‘īd (Muslim feast day):
It is an ‘īd for him whose fasting Allāh accepts and for whose prayers He is grateful; and (in fact) every day wherein no sin of Allāh is committed is an ‘īd. [1]
